what: Baseline and positive control for the zero-tolerance commit-entity census (evals/at_scale/commit_census.py). Compares what the repo holds, what the walk claims it applied, and what the graph can actually produce -- the one loss no fact-level check can see, because graph and index are consistent about a commit that was never written.
measured_by: the shipping collect_commit_census(), against the persisted graph in a separate process -- not a reimplementation, so the recorded baseline is produced by the exact function that is gated

baseline.reading: repo, walk and graph agree at 847 commits
baseline.note: The clean difference IS zero, which was the open question and is why the gate is zero-tolerance. It was PREDICTED from the code and then confirmed here, not assumed: shipping a zero-tolerance gate whose clean difference was actually nonzero is the trap #316 had to avoid with :type/external-dependency, and this issue was split out of #316 partly to avoid repeating it.

merge_commits.resolved: counted on both sides, no adjustment needed
merge_commits.evidence: frontier_registry.build_linearization is `git log --topo-order --reverse --format=%H <branch>`, the same commit set `git rev-list --count <branch>` reports. Both _forward_apply and _reverse_apply write [commit_ident :entity-type :type/commit] unconditionally as the FIRST triple in their list, before any extracted file is consulted. 66 of the 847 are merges and the census reads 0 across all three deltas.

skipped_commits.evidence: _run_ingestion's per-commit extraction handler does _ingest_progress['processed'] += 1 and `continue` from ABOVE the db lease, so nothing is written for that commit. Such a run is already failed by _exit_code's skipped_commits clause; the census fires too, independently, which is the point -- that clause is stderr-derived and reads clean when the capture itself fails.
skipped_commits.measured: 0 skipped on this run, so this path was not exercised and the baseline does not depend on it

path_ignore.evidence: the :type/commit triple is written before any extracted file is looked at, so a commit touching only ignored paths still gets its entity.

ref_mismatch.resolved: fixed at the source, and it was LIVE in this very run
ref_mismatch.evidence: _run_ingestion's repo_total was hardcoded to `git rev-list --count HEAD` while ingestion takes a branch argument. This run resolved branch to 'master' (via _default_git_branch) while the process's HEAD was the feature branch fix-317-commit-entity-census -- two different refs. They agreed at 847 here only because the feature branch carried no commits yet. Fixed to use the branch argument; the census takes its ref explicitly and never defaults it.

positive_control.resolved: shipped in the result as repo_commits, and checked
positive_control.evidence: 847 is nonzero and equals the repo's own `git rev-list --count master`. Three counts that are all zero also match perfectly, so a census over an empty repo would otherwise be indistinguishable from a census over a healthy one -- commit_census reports proved_nothing for that case and does NOT fail it, exactly as #316's code_entities_scanned == 0 renders as 'proved nothing about it'.

a_sixth_hazard_the_issue_did_not_name.detail: The commit ident is :commit/{hash[:12]}. Two commits sharing a 12-character hash prefix collapse into ONE entity, so the graph legitimately holds fewer than the repo through no fault of the write path the other deltas point at. Without a number for it the census would MISATTRIBUTE such a loss to the write path and send a reader to the wrong code.
a_sixth_hazard_the_issue_did_not_name.handling: reported as ident_collisions, still fails the gate (it is a genuine loss), and its branch is checked BEFORE the generic write-loss branch so the interpretation names the more specific cause

the_count_aggregate_finding.what: (count ?e) counts matching ROWS, not distinct entities

measured_directly_on_minigraf_2_0_0.note: The duplicate needs two DIFFERENT valid-froms. Two writes of one triple at the same valid-from collapse to a single row (back-to-back in-memory transacts read 1; the same pair 1.1s apart read 2) -- project-minigraf/minigraf#287's pending-index behaviour.

the_count_aggregate_finding.why_it_mattered_here: _count_commit_entities used (count ?e), so under it ONE duplicated commit entity CANCELS one genuinely lost commit and the census reads clean on a graph that lost history -- the precise failure the census exists to catch. Changed to (count-distinct ?e).
the_count_aggregate_finding.reachability_is_narrower_than_it_first_l: Ingestion CANNOT produce this duplicate on a commit entity: _reverse_apply and _forward_apply transact the commit triples at commit_ts_iso, the commit's own timestamp, so a resumed run re-walking a position whose _frontier_persist_claim never landed (#313) re-writes the identical triple at the identical valid-from and it collapses. The reachable path is the PUBLIC handler -- `commit` is a registered MINIGRAF_SCHEMA type, so handle_minigraf_transact writes its :entity-type at wall-clock valid-from, and two such writes seconds apart on a mixed memory-and-ingestion graph over-count.

on_this_graph.note: Latent here, not live -- consistent with the reachability above. Recorded so a future divergence between these two numbers is a signal rather than a surprise.

the_count_aggregate_finding.not_changed: _STATUS_QUERY (run_ingestion_benchmark) keeps (count ?e). Its docstring states it is deliberately frozen so the QUERY being timed stays comparable across runs; it is a latency instrument and its number is never read as a count.

the_other_gates_read_this_graph_clean.note: Not a caveat -- the point, and the same argument #316 recorded. On a graph MISSING A WHOLE COMMIT these all read clean too: fact_audit's two witnesses are written from the same triples in the same transaction boundary, so a commit that was never written is absent from BOTH and they agree perfectly; the two :introduced-by checks are well-formedness checks on entities that EXIST, and a commit that produced no entities produces nothing for either to find; and _exit_code's graph_facts == 0 clause only fires when the graph reads back COMPLETELY empty. That is why this is a separate gate clause and not a term in divergence.

cost.note: Milliseconds. It does not ride fact_audit's scan the way the two :introduced-by checks do, because it needs a repo handle fact_audit deliberately does not take -- so it is wired beside the audit rather than inside it, keeping the audit's signature honest.
